case_title: Subodh Nath and Anr. v. State of Tripura
weapon: Axe (handle recovered near body), gun, lathi/wooden stick
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW-13); corroborating witness (PW-6); inquest report and investigating officer evidence on injuries; recovery of axe handle and sticks; circumstantial evidence
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC; life imprisonment and fine of Rs.5000 each (default one year)
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence maintained
neutral_facts: The victim went out to graze cows and did not return by dusk; the next morning his body was found with injuries in a jungle. The police registered a case, held an inquest, and during investigation a labourer who worked under the victim was apprehended and made a statement implicating two men. The principal evidence is the account of an eyewitness who was grazing cows with the victim in a rubber garden around 2 p.m. At about 4 p.m. the two accused arrived armed with an axe, a lathi and a gun. The first accused struck the victim with the axe; the second struck him with a stick; and the first then took a gun from the jungle and shot him. The eyewitness fled, stating he was afraid because the accused had threatened him with dire consequences if he disclosed the incident. He later told another villager, and subsequently gave a statement to police. A witness stated that around 1.30 p.m. he had seen the victim and the accused grazing cows nearby. The investigating officer's inquest report recorded injuries caused by an axe and a gun. He also recovered the handle of an axe near the body and seized it under a seizure list prepared in the presence of witnesses. Blood-stained wooden sticks and a takkal dao were also found near the body. A charge-sheet was filed against the two accused.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from injuries caused by an axe and a gun
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness account of PW-13; corroboration by PW-6 (presence at grazing site around 1.30 p.m.); Investigating Officer's evidence and inquest report showing axe and gun injuries; seizure of axe handle
witness_credibility: PW-13 found reliable; his flight was explained by fear of the accused; discrepancies among PW-1, PW-2, PW-13 and PW-19 held not material
post_offence_conduct: Accused allegedly threatened the eyewitness with dire consequences if he disclosed the incident; the court accepted that this explained the witness leaving for Cachar
trial_duration: offence: 09.10.1998; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 08.06.2005; Supreme Court: 19.03.2013
legal_representation: Accused: Lalit Chauhan, Somanadri Goud, Kshatrashal Raj, Abhishek Vinod Deshmukh (for Parekh & Co.). State of Tripura: Ritu Raj Biswas, Gopal Singh
investigation_status: FIR registered; inquest held; witness apprehended and s.164 CrPC statement recorded; charge-sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted both under s.302/34 IPC, life imprisonment and fine. High Court: conviction and sentence maintained, appeal dismissed. Supreme Court: appellant no.1's appeal dismissed; appellant no.2's appeal allowed and remitted to the Juvenile Justice Board
prosecution_argument: Appellant no.2 was over 16 and not protected by the 2000 Act, so the conviction should stand; PW-13's evidence was corroborated by PW-6 and by the recovery of the weapons and inquest report; the disclosure-based recovery was relied on under Suresh Chandra Bahri
defence_argument: Appellant no.2 was a juvenile under the 2000 Act as amended (Hari Ram); appellant no.1's conviction rests on the sole, uncorroborated and unreliable eyewitness PW-13, who fled; discrepancies in PW-1, PW-2, PW-13 and PW-19; no recovery of weapon; motive unproved
legal_principle_applied: Discrepancies in witness testimony do not defeat evidence unless material; eyewitness evidence can be accepted if corroborated by material particulars; motive is irrelevant where direct evidence exists; juvenility under ss.7A and 20 of the 2000 Act applies to pending cases
precedent_relied_upon: State of Rajasthan v. Smt. Kalki (1981) 2 SCC 752 (relied on); Hari Ram v. State of Rajasthan (2009) 13 SCC 211 (relied on); Pratap Singh v. State of Jharkhand (2005) 3 SCC 551 (held inapplicable); Badri v. State of Rajasthan (1976) 1 SCC 442 and Lallu Manjhi v. State of Jharkhand AIR 2003 SC 854 (referred to); Suresh Chandra Bahri v. State of Bihar AIR 1994 SC 2420 (referred to)
other_sentence_order: Appellant no.2's case remitted to the Juvenile Justice Board of North Tripura district for disposal under the 2000 Act within four months
